insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Varies by plan (Silver/Gold/Platinum; Individual/Family Floater/Family First). Examples: Individual & Family Floater: Silver 2L/3L; Gold 5L-50L; Platinum 15L-1Cr. Family First: Base SI per person + Floater SI (as per Annexure II).

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Re-fill benefit Reinstate up to base Sum Insured. Applicable for same & different illness as well
great.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table (Silver/Gold/Platinum tables)
great.explanation: The policy provides an additional sum insured equal to the base amount for repeated or new illnesses after the base sum insured is exhausted. This means you get extra coverage within the same policy year for continued treatment.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: We will provide an additional re-fill amount of maximum up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: An extra sum insured equal to the base sum insured is available once per policy year after the base limit is used up. This gives you a financial cushion for additional hospitalizations.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months (under gold & platinum Plans)/ 36 months (under Silver Plans) of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months for Gold/Platinum and 36 months for Silver plans. This aligns with common market standards.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are excluded for the first 30 days except accidents, which are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period in health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: For all Insured Persons who are above 45 years of Age as on the date of inception of the First Policy with Us... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Certain illnesses have a 24-month waiting period for those over 45 years old at policy start. This is typical for specified conditions.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay above mentioned Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps cover diagnostic and treatment costs leading to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 90 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge
good.explanation: Expenses up to 90 days after discharge are covered to support recovery and follow-up care. This duration is standard in the industry.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room rent Shared Room or 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table: Individual & Family Floater Silver Plan (Renewal only)
bad.explanation: The plan restricts room rent to shared room or 1% of base sum insured per day, which can cause significant out-of-pocket expenses if you choose a higher room category.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room rent Rs 3,000 per day or Shared Room
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table: Family First - Silver Plan
bad.explanation: A daily cap of ₹3,000 or shared room eligibility limits your room choice and may reduce claim payouts if you opt for a higher room category.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the room category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligibility as specified in the Policy Schedule, then We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses
bad.explanation: If you choose a room above your plan's limit, the insurer reduces not only room rent but also related medical expenses proportionally, increasing your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: NCB
bad.quote: If the Insured Persons covered on a Family Floater Policy... Renew... by splitting... then We will provide the credit of the accumulated Cumulative Bonus to the split Policy reduced proportionately... In case the Base Sum Insured under the Policy is reduced at the time of Renewal, the applicable accumulated Cumulative Bonus shall also be reduced in proportion to the Base Sum Insured.
bad.explanation: The no-claim bonus can be reduced or lost if you reduce sum insured or split the policy, which is less favorable than policies that protect the bonus fully.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement... 6.2.14 Co-payment The Insured Person will bear a predetermined percentage of the admissible claim amounts subject to the Co-payment option chosen by You in the Proposal Form and / or Information Summary Sheet
bad.explanation: Co-payment depends on the option selected at proposal and is not clearly stated as zero or otherwise in the base policy. You must check your policy schedule to know your exact co-pay percentage.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
